title: Private Deployments - VPC & On-Prem Reference: Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades & Customer Requirements
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference guidance for private deployments (VPC and on-prem): reference architectures, packaging artifacts, day-2 operations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and the customer requirements library. Target audience: solutions engineers, SREs, and partner implementation teams responsible for onboarding and operating private deployments.

Scope

- VPC-hosted private control plane and on-prem inference clusters
- Reference architectures for small, medium, and large footprints
- Packaging format and supported OS/hypervisor images
- Day-2 operational procedures (scaling, node replacement, cert rotation, backups)
- Upgrade and rollback playbooks (canary, phased rollout, emergency rollback)
- Customer requirements checklist used during pre-sales and onboarding

Key Components and Service Names

- redwood-controller: control-plane service (API, web console)
- redwood-agent: per-customer agent for metrics, heartbeats, and config sync
- inference-node: GPU-enabled serving worker (A100/H100 optimized)
- kv-cache-service: prefix/KV cache for repeated requests
- model-repo: artifact storage for model files (S3-compatible or NFS)
- telemetry-collector: metrics/log forwarder (Prometheus + Fluentd)

Reference Architectures

1) Small (POC / single-tenant proof-of-concept)

- 1 controller vm (2 vCPU, 8GB), 1 inference-node (1 GPU - A100 40GB or equivalent), 1 storage node (NFS or S3-compatible)
- Minimum network: 1 Gbps internal networking
- Use case: non-critical evaluation, throughput < 10 rps, not expected to be multi-tenant

2) Medium (SMB / single-customer production)

- 3 controller replicas (k3s / k8s) behind LB, 3 inference nodes (2x A100/H100 recommended), HA database (Postgres 3-node), model-repo on S3 with versioning
- Network: 10 Gbps internal fabric, subnet segmentation for management / serving / storage
- Targets: 99.9% control-plane uptime, p95 latency < 300ms for typical prompts

3) Large (enterprise / multi-zone on-prem)

- Controller cluster (5+ replicas), autoscaling inference pool across 8+ GPU nodes (mixed A100/H100), distributed model-repo (object storage with cross-zone replication), dedicated kv-cache cluster, telemetry cluster with retention to long-term storage
- Targets: 99.95% uptime, p95 token latency < 200ms for short prompts, SLO for model load time < 10s for warm models

Packaging and On-Prem Artifacts

Supported packaging formats:

- OVA (VM image) for vSphere customers
- AMI-like QCOW2 images for private cloud / OpenStack
- Docker images + Helm charts for k8s-based installs (Helm v3, Kubernetes v1.25+ supported)
- Installer bundles: redwood-onprem-<version>.tar.gz containing manifests, operator, and validation scripts

Supported base OS / runtime:

| Component | Supported OS / Runtime | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Controller | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS | systemd service, uses Postgres 13+ |
| Inference node | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS + NVIDIA drivers | CUDA 12+, cuDNN compatibles; H100 recommended for production |
| Model-repo gateway | MinIO / S3-compatible | Versioning and lifecycle required |

Packaging checklist (pre-release):

- [ ] Signed packages and checksums (SHA256)
- [ ] Upgrade scripts included and tested (dry-run mode)
- [ ] Health-check and smoke-test scripts
- [ ] Packaging includes RBAC manifests and sample network policies

Network & Security Requirements

Minimum network rules (example):

- Controller API: TCP 8443 (inbound from admin subnet)
- redwood-agent heartbeat: TCP/UDP 50051 outbound to controller cluster
- Inference node serving: TCP 8080 (internal), optional TLS termination on 443
- Model-repo (S3): TCP 9000/443 depending on endpoint
- KV cache (Redis-like): TCP 6379 internal-only

Firewall rules guidance:

1) Deny all ingress to inference-node port 8080 from public; only controller and internal load balancers allowed.
2) Allow controller admin access only from customer admin CIDR and Redwood support IPs when authorized.

Identity & Key Management

- KMS: Customers must provide a KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM) for encryption of at-rest secrets; integration using redwood-kms-adapter (configurable in values.yaml).
- TLS: All inter-service communication must be TLS 1.2+; certificates can be managed by customer (recommended) or via our ACME integration in air-gapped-friendly mode.

Storage & Backups

- Model artifacts: stored in S3-compatible storage with versioning. Retention policy configurable per-customer.
- Database backups: automated daily logical backups (pg_dump) and WAL shipping for point-in-time recovery. Target RPO: 1 hour, RTO: 2 hours for control-plane.
- Snapshot checklist:
  1. Validate backup completion in telemetry
  2. Store encrypted backups to customer-managed object storage
  3. Test restore quarterly in a staging environment

Day-2 Operations (Runbook Highlights)

Ownership and contacts

- Primary: eng-private-deployments (oncall rotation)
- Escalation: Solutions Engineering -> Eng SRE -> Product -> Security for incidents
- PagerDuty: team-redwood-private-deployments

Common day-2 tasks

- Scaling inference pool: use redwood-controller autoscaler to add nodes; recommended CPU/GPU utilization thresholds: scale-out at GPU util > 70% sustained for 5 minutes, scale-in when < 30% for 10 minutes.
- Replacing failed node: cordon -> drain -> delete -> provision replacement image -> join cluster.
- Certificate rotation: run ./scripts/rotate-certs.sh on controller cluster during maintenance window, verify services with smoke tests.
- Log retention & troubleshooting: Fluentd forwards to customer ELK or Splunk; ensure 30d default retention for logs and 90d for aggregated metrics if required.

Monitoring & Alerts (recommended thresholds)

- Control-plane API error rate > 5% (5m window): Sev2
- Inference-node GPU memory OOM events: Sev1
- Model load time > 30s for 3+ models: Sev2
- Disk usage > 80% on model-repo: Notify and run cleanup lifecycle

Upgrade Procedure (standard, non-emergency)

Pre-upgrade (preflight)

1. Review release notes and changelog.
2. Confirm backups for Postgres, model-repo, and configuration.
3. Run preflight validation: ./validate-deployment.sh --dry-run; address failures.
4. Schedule maintenance window; notify stakeholders and record expected rollback plan.

Canary / Phased rollout

1. Deploy controller vX.Y to 1 canary controller replica (25% traffic) with feature-flag off.
2. Run smoke tests: API health, basic inference against golden prompt set, metrics ingestion.
3. If canary succeeds for 30m with no errors and p95 latency within 10% of baseline, promote next batch to 50% traffic.
4. Roll inference-node runtime images using rolling update with maxUnavailable=1 per AZ.

Post-upgrade validation

- Run baseline eval suite (10 representative prompt sets) and compare token-level quality metrics.
- Confirm model load & KV-cache warm times.
- Monitor for regressions for 48 hours; hold for human sign-off for risky changes (model weights format, quantization changes).

Rollback Procedure (if canary/upgrade fails)

1. Abort promotion and immediately stop traffic to new controllers via LB or routing policy.
2. Revert controller image to previous tag using kubectl rollout undo or restore from pre-upgrade snapshot.
3. Restore Postgres from the most recent logical backup if schema migration failed.
4. If model-repo artifacts are incompatible, switch to read-only mode and serve from cached model mirrors until artifacts are restored.
5. Post-rollback: create incident report, include root-cause analysis, and schedule a follow-up patch release.

Emergency rollback (fast path)

- If severe Sev1 (complete control-plane outage), use emergency rollback runbook: immediate LB failover to secondary region or standby controllers; if unavailable, enable offline inference mode (local-only serving) and restore control-plane later.

Upgrade testing checklist

- [ ] Canary passed smoke tests (API, inference, metrics)
- [ ] No critical errors in logs for 30 minutes
- [ ] Baseline eval shows no more than 2% regression in quality metrics per prompt set
- [ ] Backups are verified and retrievable

Customer Requirements Library (Pre-sales & Onboarding Checklist)

Use this table during discovery. Fields are minimum requirements; mark optional items during contract negotiation.

| Requirement area | Minimum requirement | Typical customer response / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Network | Internal CIDR, management CIDR, outbound internet for telemetry optional | Provide firewall rules, NAT gateway details |
| Compute | GPU type (A100/H100) and count, CPU/RAM for controller | Customers often specify cost vs latency tradeoffs |
| Storage | S3-compatible endpoint with versioning and >= 1TB initial capacity | Confirm encryption at rest and lifecycle policies |
| IAM | Service accounts and roles for redwood-controller and agents | RBAC mapping for admin, ops, read-only roles |
| KMS | Customer-managed KMS or allow Redwood-adapter integration | Required for enterprise customers with PCI/PHI |
| Compliance | SOC2 / ISO / FedRAMP needs | Confirm evidence package and audit window |
| Maintenance Windows | Weekly maintenance window (2 hours) and emergency contact | Agree on blackout windows for training jobs |
| Network Egress | Estimated egress per month (GB) | Used to size network and cost expectations |

Onboarding steps (numbered)

1. Discovery call: collect network, compute, storage, IAM & KMS requirements.
2. Provision pre-prod environment with minimal footprint for validation.
3. Run deployment with customer-provided artifacts and perform smoke tests.
4. Execute load testing (targeted 2x expected traffic) and quality evals.
5. Sign-off and schedule production cutover with rollback plan.

Appendices

A - Useful commands

- Preflight validation: ./validate-deployment.sh --cluster mycluster --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig
- Upgrade controller: helm upgrade redwood-controller ./charts/controller --namespace redwood --set image.tag=vX.Y
- Rollback controller: kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/redwood-controller
- Drain node: kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

B - Smoke test sample (bash)

curl -s -k -X POST https://controller.internal:8443/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":20}' | jq .
